  "text": "The council replaced our streetlights on a Tuesday. By Wednesday, everyone’s shadow pointed towards my house.

At noon, people stopped outside my gate and turned slowly, watching the dark shapes pivot beneath them.

I closed the curtains.

A council engineer came on Friday. He checked the nearest lamp, then asked to use my toilet.

After twenty minutes, I knocked.

He was standing in the hallway, staring at a photograph of my mother.

“Does she live here?”

“She died in March.”

He looked down. His shadow stretched across the carpet and disappeared beneath the cellar door.

“You should turn the lights off,” he said.

“Which ones?”

He left without answering.

That evening, the shadows began arriving without their owners.

They slipped under the front door, narrow and patient. Some paused beside the coat hooks, as though remembering something they had meant to bring.

All of them went downstairs.

I called the police. While I waited, I found the cellar key in the kitchen drawer, beneath my mother’s hospital bracelet.

She had lived with me for eleven years. I had never given her a key.

Below the cellar door, light showed through the gap.

I heard chairs scraping. A spoon tapped a cup.

Then my mother called my name.

I put the key into the lock but didn’t turn it.

“You can come down,” she said. “I’ve told them everything.”

Behind me, my own shadow rose against the wall.

It reached past my shoulder and turned the key.

From downstairs came the sound my mother used to make when I returned late: one relieved breath, then the careful setting down of her cup."
